chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:
I was having dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when he recited this Verse:
But! The human being is evidence against himself * Although he puts forth his excuses
O Abu Hafs! What is the human doing if he apologises to the people with against what Allah knows from him.
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saying: ‘The one does something secretly, Allah would Clothe it in return – if good, so good, and if evil, so evil’.

key_terms.رِدَاءَهَا: His clothing of it (metaphor for manifestation)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Allah clothing a person with their secret actions?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, the Imam (peace be upon him) elucidates the verse from Surah al-Qiyamah, explaining that human self-witnessing (basirah) renders external excuses futile since Allah knows the inner reality. He connects this to the Prophetic tradition that one's secret intentions are manifested externally as a 'garment' of their true nature, a concept central to Shia teachings on sincerity (ikhlas) and the transition from inner state to outer action.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,
‘I was having dinner with Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> when he recited this Verse
[75:14] But! The human being is evidence against himself [75:15] Although he puts forth his excuses.

(He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said): ‘O Abu Hafs! What is the human doing if he apologises to the people with against what Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Knows from him.

Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> was saying: ‘The one does something secretly, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Clothe it in return – if good, so good, and if evil, so evil’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “
Once I was having dinner with abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and he read this verse of the Holy Quran:
‘In fact, people are well aware of their own soul [75:14] even though they make excuses.’ [75:15]
The Imam said, ‘O abu Hafs, why should a human being make excuses before the people, opposing what Allah knows about him (his intention being to show off)?
The Messenger of Allah has said, “Whoever does a deed secretly Allah will make him wear its (the deed’s) garment as good rewards were it a good deed, and in an evil form were it an evil deed.’”
